_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::particle_pd#9. Both halves of the rule hold and both quoted Signals are wrong. (a) POS is a fixed-size 3-vector, so dropping z makes the parser take the next token as the missing component and fail on IT: "Could not parse 'PDBODYID' as a double value." from core/io/src/4C_io_value_parser.cpp line 107 — the message blames the optional state after POS, never mentions coordinates, and there is no 'expected 3 coordinates' string in 4C. (b) a zero z-extent in DOMAINBOUNDINGBOX does not 'conflict with binning' politely: 4C divides the domain length by the bin size and dies inside ParticleEngine::init_binning_strategy with Signal: Floating point exception (8) / divide-by-zero (3), no PROC 0 ERROR block, no message, exit status 136 rather than 1 — so an agent watching for a non-zero-but-normal exit and a diagnostic gets neither. The thin-slab arm is the control and passes. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: Could not parse 'PDBODYID' as a double value.

_mutation.note: remove the first pathology: keep the z coordinate on the particle line. The parse error vanishes and EXIT_TWOCOORD becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the second pathology: keep the thin-slab z extent. The divide-by-zero and its signal vanish and EXIT_FLATBOX becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
